t: Between 1580 and the 1820s well over a million people from present-day Angola were shipped as slaves to the New World, mainly to Brazil, and Oliver and Atmore called the colony 'a gigantic slave-trading enterprise' for 200 years.

Portugal ruled only the coast in the 16th and 17th centuries; full control of the territory came at the beginning of the 20th century, through wars of conquest and agreements with other European powers.
Forced labour lasted until 1962, and the war for independence that began in 1961 ended only after the Carnation Revolution in Lisbon, with independence on 11 November 1975.
dyk: From 1640 to 1648 Luanda was Dutch, ruled as Fort Aardenburgh: the Dutch, who had seized north-eastern Brazil, wanted slaves for its sugarcane plantations.
ev: Paulo Dias de Novais founds the settlement of São Paulo de Loanda, Luanda, on the coast south of the Kingdom of Kongo
The Dutch hold Luanda as Fort Aardenburgh until Portugal re-establishes its authority
Portugal defeats the Kingdom of Kongo at the Battle of Mbwila, but suffers a disastrous defeat at the Battle of Kitombo when it invades Kongo in 1670
The slave trade is abolished, badly damaging the colony's economy; Angola's ports are opened to legal foreign shipping in 1844
Agreements with the Congo Free State, the German Empire and France fix most of the colony's borders
General António Júlio da Costa Pereira de Eça's campaign reoccupies southern Angola after the German-backed Ovambo Uprising
Holden Roberto's incursion of 15 March opens the war for independence; the same year the Estatuto do Indigenato is abolished
On 11 November Angola becomes a sovereign state under the Alvor Agreement, as the People's Republic of Angola

f.capital: Luanda (São Paulo de Luanda; held by the Dutch as Fort Aardenburgh, 1640–1648)
f.founder: Paulo Dias de Novais, who founded Luanda in 1575
f.predecessor: The Kingdom of Kongo and the Kingdom of Ndongo; other polities of the region such as the Kingdom of Lunda, the Mbunda Kingdom, Bié and Bailundo
f.successor: The People's Republic of Angola (11 November 1975)
